correctness.rationale: The direct definition and independent streaming update give identical signatures on all 123032 words over alphabets of size 2 through 5 at lengths one through seven. Exhaustive binary lists establish no ambiguity at lengths 3-5, 3 double fibers at length 6 with 3 occurrences of each symbol, and 10 at length 7 with at least two occurrences of each symbol. Equality of q-ary decks survives every binary indicator projection. Any changed q-ary symbol must then occur at least twice for length 7, forcing at most three changed symbols and at most five total used symbols; for length 6 two changed symbols of frequency 3 exhaust all positions. The exhaustive five-letter length-7 census (78125 words) therefore closes the infinite-alphabet quantifier. All its fibers have size at most two; exactly ten use each pair and fifteen each triple, with none on larger support. The capacity count is one representative per fiber. The packaged standard-library verifier runs to the reported pass sentinel.

originality.rationale: The source paper explicitly reports the binary threshold G(2)=6, which is credited. The new claim is the exact full alphabet-uniform fiber/capacity spectrum at lengths 1-7, especially 15 length-seven double fibers per unordered three-symbol support and the support cutoff. The inspected source sections concern collision thresholds and asymptotic constructions, without counting all q-ary short fibers; distinct ungapped-deck or contiguous-substring formulas do not imply the gapped-pair counts. Database comparisons identified related different-readout results rather than a covering statement. An unindexed equivalent enumeration remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The invariant N_q(n) is the exact maximum size of a distinguishable q-ary reconstruction code from skipped-position two-subsequence readouts, a natural short-read DNA/data-storage statistic. The proof gives a complete nontrivial length-seven fiber classification for every alphabet, with the first genuinely ternary collision count and a finite support bound that prevents an unjustified extrapolation from binary values. It is a complete structural finite-length boundary, not an isolated convenient numerical slice; it does not claim a longer-length asymptotic.
